relations.title: Connect an Entra sign-in to GraphAPIAuditEvents
relations.description: Match the Entra sign-in token ID with UniqueTokenIdentifier in the Defender XDR GraphAPIAuditEvents table.
relations.guidance: Compare non-empty token identifiers exactly and preserve case; never lowercase a UTI. One token can have many activity records. Keep actor, tenant, application, and time context, and include the originating sign-in in the lookback. A missing match can reflect retention or collection gaps.

otherNotes.title: Use the token ID to trace a sign-in session
otherNotes.text: GraphAPIAuditEvents.UniqueTokenIdentifier can be matched to the unique token identifier on an Entra sign-in record. In Defender XDR, this relationship is represented by EntraIdSignInEvents.UniqueTokenId. The matching sign-in can give you session context for investigating other activity. If you also query Sentinel sign-in tables, include interactive, non-interactive, service principal, and managed identity sign-ins for broader coverage. Keep user and application identities distinct when enriching results, and treat missing sign-in matches as a lead to investigate rather than proof of malicious activity.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Graph API activity logs — Part 3
otherNotes.query:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(UniqueTokenIdentifier)
| join kind=inner (EntraIdSignInEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where isnotempty(UniqueTokenId)
    | project SignInTime=Timestamp, UniqueTokenId
) on $left.UniqueTokenIdentifier == $right.UniqueTokenId
| project GraphTime=Timestamp, UniqueTokenIdentifier, RequestUri, RequestMethod, AccountObjectId, SignInTime
| order by GraphTime desc

otherNotes.title: Normalize Graph requests before comparing activity
otherNotes.text: When looking for automated discovery, compare endpoint patterns rather than raw request URLs. Replace object IDs in the path and remove query strings so requests for different objects collapse into the same pattern. Compare volume and endpoint combinations against a baseline for the account or application. UserAgent is not available in this GraphAPIAuditEvents schema; where another Graph log source provides it, remember that it can be changed and use it only as supporting context.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Graph API activity logs — Part 1
otherNotes.query:
GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| extend ActorId = coalesce(AccountObjectId, ServicePrincipalId, ApplicationId)
| extend NormalizedRequestUri = replace_regex(RequestUri, @'[0-9a-fA-F]{8}\b-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\b-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\b-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}\b-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}', @'<UUID>')
| extend NormalizedRequestUri = replace_regex(NormalizedRequestUri, @'\?.*$', @'')
| summarize RequestCount=count(), Endpoints=make_set(NormalizedRequestUri, 100), IPAddresses=make_set(IpAddress, 100) by ActorId, EntityType
| order by RequestCount desc

relations.description: Compare the Entra sign-in token ID with SignInActivityId in the Sentinel MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs table.
relations.guidance: Compare non-empty token identifiers exactly and preserve case; never lowercase a UTI. One token can have many activity records. Keep actor, tenant, application, and time context, and include the originating sign-in in the lookback. A missing match can reflect retention or collection gaps.

otherNotes.title: Keep user and application identities distinct
otherNotes.text: In MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs, the actor ID may be in UserId or ServicePrincipalId. Preserve which field supplied the value when enriching or grouping activity. For broader Sentinel sign-in coverage, the article unions interactive, non-interactive, service principal, and managed identity sign-in tables. Those Sentinel tables are separate from EntraIdSignInEvents in Defender XDR.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Graph API activity logs — Part 2
otherNotes.query:
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| extend ObjectId = iff(isempty(UserId), ServicePrincipalId, UserId)
| extend ObjectType = iff(isempty(UserId), "ServicePrincipalId", "UserId")
| summarize Requests=count(), Endpoints=dcount(RequestUri) by ObjectType, ObjectId
| order by Requests desc

otherNotes.title: Normalize request URLs and baseline activity
otherNotes.text: For reconnaissance hunts, compare normalized endpoint patterns and request volume by actor. Replace object IDs in URLs and remove query strings before comparing paths. User agents can be changed, and normal activity varies between environments, so treat tool fingerprints and unusual patterns as investigation leads and build a local baseline.

otherNotes.title: Expand Graph batch requests
otherNotes.text: Microsoft Graph batch activity may include a record for the POST to $batch and separate records for the individual requests. The article uses OperationId to group the batch with its component requests, which can reveal the actual endpoints involved.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Graph API activity logs — Part 2
otherNotes.query:
let BatchRequests = MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RequestMethod == "POST" and RequestUri endswith "/$batch"
| project OperationId, BatchTime=TimeGenerated, BatchRequestUri=RequestUri;
MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where RequestMethod != "POST"
| join kind=inner BatchRequests on OperationId
| project BatchTime, TimeGenerated, OperationId, BatchRequestUri, RequestUri, RequestMethod
| order by BatchTime desc

relations.title: Connect an Entra sign-in to AADGraphActivityLogs
relations.description: Compare EntraIdSignInEvents.UniqueTokenId with SignInActivityId in the separate Sentinel AADGraphActivityLogs table.
relations.guidance: Compare non-empty token identifiers exactly and preserve case; never lowercase a UTI. One token can have many activity records. Keep actor, tenant, application, and time context, and include the originating sign-in in the lookback. A missing match can reflect retention or collection gaps. AAD Graph SignInActivityId is a best-effort token link. Exact equality can miss padded values. Remove only trailing Base64 padding on both sides and preserve case. This does not convert GUID-shaped IDs to Base64 or equate them with sign-in Id/CorrelationId. Inspect unmatched GUID-shaped values separately. TimeRequested is the request time; allow for delayed ingestion.

otherNotes.title: Account for request and record time differences
otherNotes.text: TimeRequested is when the API call occurred, while TimeGenerated is when the log record was generated. The article observed a median gap of about seven minutes and a maximum of 70 minutes in its lab. Measure the delay in your own data and use an appropriate time window when investigating related sign-ins.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Now You See Me — AADGraphActivityLogs
otherNotes.query:
AADGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend RequestDelay = TimeGenerated - TimeRequested
| summarize MedianDelay=percentile(RequestDelay, 50), MaximumDelay=max(RequestDelay), Events=count()

otherNotes.title: Pivot from AAD Graph activity to the sign-in
otherNotes.text: Invictus IR describes correlating AADGraphActivityLogs.SignInActivityId with SigninLogs.UniqueTokenIdentifier after removing trailing token padding. This adapted example uses EntraIdSignInEvents.UniqueTokenId in Defender. Preserve identifier case and verify the formats in your own data; padding normalization does not convert GUID-shaped values into token identifiers.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Invictus IR: The missing link — AADGraphActivityLogs finally arrives
otherNotes.query:
let LeftEvents = EntraIdSignInEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend LeftKey = trim_end(@"=+", tostring(UniqueTokenId))
| where isnotempty(LeftKey);
let RightEvents = AADGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeRequested > ago(7d)
| extend RightKey = trim_end(@"=+", tostring(SignInActivityId))
| where isnotempty(RightKey);
LeftEvents
| join kind=inner (RightEvents) on $left.LeftKey == $right.RightKey
| project-away LeftKey, RightKey

otherNotes.title: SignInActivityId formats
otherNotes.text: SignInActivityId can contain padded token identifiers and GUID-shaped values. Remove trailing Base64 padding when correlating token identifiers and preserve case. Padding removal does not convert GUID-shaped values into token identifiers. Inspect unmatched GUID-shaped values separately.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Now You See Me — AADGraphActivityLogs
otherNotes.query:
AADGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| summarize by SignInActivityId
| summarize
    Padded=countif(SignInActivityId endswith "=="),
    GUID=countif(SignInActivityId matches regex @"^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$"),

relations.guidance: Compare non-empty token identifiers exactly and preserve case; never lowercase a UTI. One token can have many activity records. Keep actor, tenant, application, and time context, and include the originating sign-in in the lookback. A missing match can reflect retention or collection gaps.

relations.title: Follow AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs tokens into AADGraphActivityLogs
relations.description: Match AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs.UniqueTokenIdentifier to AADGraphActivityLogs.SignInActivityId for token-level activity correlation.
relations.guidance: Compare non-empty token identifiers exactly and preserve case; never lowercase a UTI. One token can have many activity records. Keep actor, tenant, application, and time context, and include the originating sign-in in the lookback. A missing match can reflect retention or collection gaps. AAD Graph SignInActivityId is a best-effort token link. Exact equality can miss padded values. Remove only trailing Base64 padding on both sides and preserve case. This does not convert GUID-shaped IDs to Base64 or equate them with sign-in Id/CorrelationId. Inspect unmatched GUID-shaped values separately. TimeRequested is the request time; allow for delayed ingestion.
relations.kql:
let LeftEvents = AADManagedIdentitySignInLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| extend LeftKey = trim_end(@"=+", tostring(UniqueTokenIdentifier))
| where isnotempty(LeftKey);
let RightEvents = AADGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeRequested > ago(7d)
| extend RightKey = trim_end(@"=+", tostring(SignInActivityId))
| where isnotempty(RightKey);
LeftEvents
| join kind=inner (RightEvents) on $left.LeftKey == $right.RightKey
| project-away LeftKey, RightKey

otherNotes.title: SignInActivityId formats
otherNotes.text: SignInActivityId can contain padded token identifiers and GUID-shaped values. Remove trailing Base64 padding when correlating token identifiers and preserve case. Padding removal does not convert GUID-shaped values into token identifiers. Inspect unmatched GUID-shaped values separately.
otherNotes.sourceLabel: Cloudbrothers: Now You See Me — AADGraphActivityLogs
otherNotes.query:
AADGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
| summarize by SignInActivityId
| summarize
    Padded=countif(SignInActivityId endswith "=="),
    GUID=countif(SignInActivityId matches regex @"^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$"),
    TotalUnique=dcount(SignInActivityId)

relations.title: Follow a process into DeviceNetworkEvents

Require activity at or after ProcessCreationTime. Extend the process lookback when a long-running parent predates the activity window. These fields can be empty on unsupported platforms.
relations.kql:
let Processes = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(DeviceId) and isnotempty(ProcessUniqueId)
| project TenantId, DeviceId, ProcessKey=ProcessUniqueId, ProcessStart=ProcessCreationTime,
          ProcessEventTime=Timestamp, ProcessFile=FileName, ProcessCommandLine;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where isnotempty(DeviceId) and isnotempty(InitiatingProcessUniqueId)
| extend ProcessKey=InitiatingProcessUniqueId, ActivityTime=Timestamp
| join kind=inner (Processes) on TenantId, DeviceId, ProcessKey
| where ActivityTime >= ProcessStart

DeviceProcessEvents

| extend FileKey=tolower(SHA1)

relations.title: Link Entra sign-ins to beta sign-in sessions
relations.description: Match the authentication session ID between EntraIdSignInEvents and AADSignInEventsBeta.
relations.guidance: AADSignInEventsBeta is deprecated. The two tables can expose the same authentication session identifiers for retained records. Prefer EntraIdSignInEvents for current data; treat matches as one-to-many, exclude empty values, and retain AccountObjectId and time context when joining.

| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(AccountObjectId) and isnotempty(SessionId)
| summarize by AccountObjectId, SessionId;
let BetaSessions = AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(AccountObjectId) and isnotempty(SessionId)

relations.title: Relate the two beta sign-in device ID fields
relations.description: Compare AadDeviceId and EntraIdDeviceId within AADSignInEventsBeta.
relations.guidance: AADSignInEventsBeta is deprecated. These fields may represent aliases for the same Entra device identifier in retained beta records. Prefer current Entra sign-in schemas when available, compare non-empty values before relying on the alias, and preserve both source field names because schema aliases can vary by table version.
relations.kql:
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(AadDeviceId) and isnotempty(EntraIdDeviceId)
| extend AadHash = hash_sha256(tostring(AadDeviceId)), EntraHash = hash_sha256(tostring(EntraIdDeviceId))
| summarize Rows = count(), Different = countif(AadHash != EntraHash)

relations.title: Correlate Microsoft Graph requests across audit sources
relations.description: Match the same Microsoft Graph RequestUri between GraphAPIAuditEvents and MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs.
relations.guidance: The same Microsoft Graph request may be represented in both sources. RequestUri is not globally unique, so retain request method, actor, application, and a narrow time window; normalize object IDs only for endpoint-pattern analysis, not exact event correlation.
relations.kql:
let GraphAudit = GraphAPIAuditEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(RequestUri)
| project RequestUri, AccountObjectId, RequestMethod, AuditTime = Timestamp;
let GraphActivity = MicrosoftGraphActivityLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where isnotempty(RequestUri)
| project RequestUri, UserId, RequestMethod, ActivityTime = TimeGenerated;
GraphAudit
| join kind=inner GraphActivity on RequestUri, RequestMethod
| project RequestUri, RequestMethod, AccountObjectId, UserId, AuditTime, ActivityTime

| mv-expand TargetResource = TargetResources
| extend JoinKey = tostring(TargetResource.id)
| where isnotempty(JoinKey);
let RightEvents = IdentityInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend JoinKey = tostring(AccountObjectId)
| where isnotempty(JoinKey);
LeftEvents
| join kind=inner (RightEvents) on JoinKey
